program_full_name: Pre-Admission Screening System Providing Options and Resources Today
administered_by: the Ohio Department of Aging, through regional Area Agencies on Aging that assign each participant a case manager
eligibility_threshold: Ohio does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. Participants must be age 60 or older, be frail enough to require a nursing home level of care, and be able to remain safely at home with their physician's consent.
asset_limit_single: Not published on the cited Ohio Department of Aging page; set by Ohio Medicaid institutional-care financial eligibility rules
asset_limit_couple: Not published on the cited page; spousal rules apply
look_back_period: Not published on the cited page; standard Medicaid transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: A local Area Agency on Aging screens the applicant and, once eligible, assigns a case manager who builds the in-home service package with local providers and checks in on quality.
unique_feature: PASSPORT is delivered through the regional Area Agency on Aging rather than a statewide office, so the same program is administered by the agency covering your county, and a case manager stays involved after enrollment to adjust the service package.

program_full_name: Community First Choice and the Community Options Program Entry System
administered_by: the Aging and Long-Term Support Administration at the Washington State Department of Social and Health Services, through local Home and Community Services offices
eligibility_threshold: Washington does not publish a separate, lower functional threshold for dementia. Both programs require a nursing-facility level of care determined by assessment; COPES is generally provided to people already enrolled in Community First Choice.
asset_limit_single: Not published on the cited DSHS page; set by Washington Apple Health long-term care financial eligibility rules
asset_limit_couple: Not published on the cited DSHS page; spousal impoverishment rules apply
look_back_period: Not published on the cited page; standard Medicaid transfer-of-asset rules apply
application_process: Apply at a local Home and Community Services office, by requesting a paper application, or online at washingtonconnection.org. Community Living Connections (waclc.org, 1-855-567-0252) is the state's entry point for finding services.
unique_feature: Community First Choice lets participants choose who provides their care, including hiring family members as paid caregivers. Washington also runs a Medicaid Specialized Dementia Care Program, a dementia-specific benefit most states do not have.
